sentences.text: Kael is a young warrior.
He lives in a small village.
An old woman, Elara, is his teacher.
She trained him in secret.
Kael is brave and strong.
The village has a special stone.
It is the Sunstone.
The stone gives light and warmth to everyone.
It is very important.
But last week, there was a problem.
An evil sorcerer named Malakor came.
He stole the Sunstone.
Now, the village is cold and dark.
The people are scared and sad.
Elara talked to Kael yesterday.
"You must get the stone back," she said.
"Malakor's fortress is far away.
The journey is dangerous.
You should be very careful."
Kael took his father's sword and a small bag with food.
He started his quest.
He walked into the Dark Forest.
The trees were tall and black.
He saw big spiders, but he was not afraid.
He walked quietly.
Soon, he came to a wide river.
A big, green troll was under a bridge.
"Stop!" the troll shouted.
"This is my bridge."
The troll looked very angry.
Kael was smart.
He did not want to fight.
He had a shiny blue rock in his bag.
He gave the rock to the troll.
"This is a gift for you," Kael said.
The troll liked the rock.
"You can pass," the troll said with a big smile.
Kael finally saw the Shadow Fortress.
It was a very big and dark castle.
The main door was open.
He went inside very quietly.
He saw Malakor in a large room.
The sorcerer was looking at the Sunstone.
The stone was shining brightly.
Kael had a plan.
He needed to be fast.
He ran, grabbed the Sunstone, and ran out of the fortress.
"Hey!" shouted Malakor.
But Kael was already gone.
Kael ran back home.
The Sunstone was warm in his hands.
Its light made the forest bright.
The spiders ran away from it.
When he arrived at his village, everyone cheered.
They were so happy.
Kael put the Sunstone back in its place.
The village was warm and light again.
Kael was the hero of his village.
